{{nihongo|'''Ogawa Shrine'''|小川神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

'''Ogawa Shrine''' (おがわじんじゃ) is a shrine located at Oneyama 6862, {{ill|lt=Ogawa, Nagano|Q1348971|qid=Q1348971|1=Ogawa, Nagano}}, {{ill|lt=Kamiminochi District|Q1155074|qid=Q1155074|1=Kamiminochi District, Nagano}}, {{ill|lt=Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877|1=Nagano Prefecture}}. It is a debated identification for a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ronsha. It was formerly called Ōmiya Daimyōjin and Suwa Daimyōjingū<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>.

=== Overview ===
It was formerly known as Ōmiya Daimyōjin and Suwa Daimyōjingū. Shrine traditions and old records were lost in the {{ill|lt=Meiwa|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161|1=Meiwa}} era. In addition, in {{ill|lt=1933|Q18726|qid=Q18726|1=1933}} (Shōwa 8), a fire at the shrine household destroyed written materials and old documents, including a permit issued by the {{ill|lt=Yoshida family|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722|1=Yoshida family}} in {{ill|lt=1790|Q7775|qid=Q7775|1=1790}} (Kansei 2). According to legend, the beginning was when Ogawa Mahito, a local magnate of Furuyama in Ogawa Village and a sake brewer, worshipped his ancestor {{ill|lt=Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277|lt=Oto no Ōdo no Mikoto|1=Emperor Keitai}} as the tutelary deity of Oneyama in Ogawa Village. Descendants of Ogawa Mahito built a fort at Furuyama and took the name Ogawa clan. In the {{ill|lt=Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}, {{ill|lt=Ogawa Sadatsuna|UNKNOWN|lt=Ogawa Saemon Sadatsuna}} earned distinction in the {{ill|lt=Jōkyū War|Q1372308|qid=Q1372308|1=Jōkyū War}}, became {{ill|lt=jitō|Q1329805|qid=Q1329805|1=Jitō}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ogawa-shō|1=UNKNOWN}}, ruled 3,000 koku of Ogawa-go as lord of {{ill|lt=Ogawa Castle|Q11460417|qid=Q11460417|1=Ogawa Castle}}, and repaired the shrine buildings. When the Ogawa clan was defeated in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōnin War|1=UNKNOWN}}, the shrine buildings fell into ruin. Later, in {{ill|lt=1536|Q6457|qid=Q6457|1=1536}} (Tenbun 5), {{ill|lt=Ōhigata Nagamasa|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōhigata Danjō Masatada Kogorō Nagamasa}} came to rule Ogawa Village and the shrine was revived. The former shrine site was at Miyahira, on a hill next to the present site, known as a moon-viewing spot; when the Ōhigata clan developed the current site and moved the shrine there, only Oyama Shrine remained at the former site, and later that precinct land was used for school buildings and merged into this shrine. In {{ill|lt=1598|Q6800|qid=Q6800|1=1598}} (Keichō 3), when {{ill|lt=Uesugi Kagekatsu|Q1376605|qid=Q1376605|1=Uesugi Kagekatsu}} was transferred to {{ill|lt=Aizu|Q1205071|qid=Q1205071|1=Aizu}}, the {{ill|lt=Ōhigata clan|Q11435635|qid=Q11435635|1=Ōhigata clan}} also became {{ill|lt=rōnin|Q212418|qid=Q212418|1=Rōnin}} and settled locally, Furuyama Castle was abandoned, and the shrine household dispersed. In August {{ill|lt=1790|Q7775|qid=Q7775|1=1790}} (Kansei 2), the shrine petitioned the {{ill|lt=Yoshida family|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722|1=Yoshida family}} for an official declaration and, after receiving the notice, changed its name from Ōmiya Daimyōjin / Suwa Daimyōjingū to Ogawa Shrine. In January {{ill|lt=1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720|1=1869}} (Meiji 2), it became a prayer site of {{ill|lt=Kachō-no-miya|Q11620129|qid=Q11620129|1=Kachō-no-miya}} and received imperial curtain and lantern items with the reverse chrysanthemum crest. In {{ill|lt=1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753|1=1872}} (Meiji 5), its 2-koku shrine estate was confiscated, and in June {{ill|lt=1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757|1=1873}} (Meiji 6) it was ranked as a village shrine, then promoted to gōsha on November 30, {{ill|lt=1920|Q2155|qid=Q2155|1=1920}} (Taishō 9)<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>.
The present main sanctuary was built in October {{ill|lt=1729|Q6952|qid=Q6952|1=1729}} (Kyōhō 14), and the roofed main hall plus heiden/haiden were newly rebuilt in {{ill|lt=1956|Q5221|qid=Q5221|1=1956}} (Shōwa 31)<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>.

{{ill|lt=Ogawa, Nagano|Q1348971|qid=Q1348971|1=Ogawa, Nagano}} also has {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sawanomiya Ogawa Shrine|1=UNKNOWN}}, another debated candidate for the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. According to a document dated April {{ill|lt=1768|Q7675|qid=Q7675|1=1768}} (Meiwa 5), both Ogawa Shrines shared the same priest (Sakai Nagato), parishioners, and enshrined deity; although the order of their foundations is unknown, they are considered to have originally formed one unit as inner and outer shrine sites<ref>戸谷一郎『精説長野県史』123頁（日本精神文化研究所、1962年）</ref>.

'''小川神社'''（おがわじんじゃ）は、{{ill|lt=長野県|Q127877|qid=Q127877|1=Nagano Prefecture}}{{ill|lt=上水内郡|Q1155074|qid=Q1155074|1=Kamiminochi District, Nagano}}{{ill|lt=小川村|Q1348971|qid=Q1348971|1=Ogawa, Nagano}}小根山6862にある神社。{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}論社。かつては大宮大明神、諏訪大明神宮と呼ばれた<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>。

===概要===
かつては大宮大明神、諏訪大明神宮と呼ばれていた。社伝や旧記は{{ill|lt=明和|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161|1=Meiwa}}年間に流失した。また、{{ill|lt=昭和|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}8年（{{ill|lt=1933年|Q18726|qid=Q18726|1=1933}}）には社家が火災に遭遇したため、{{ill|lt=寛政|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}2年（{{ill|lt=1790年|Q7775|qid=Q7775|1=1790}}）の{{ill|lt=吉田家|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722|1=Yoshida family}}による許状などといった記述書類・古文書等を焼失してしまったが、伝説によると、小川村古山の豪族・酒人小川真人が小川村小根山の産土神として自らの祖である{{ill|lt=継体天皇|Q349277|qid=Q349277|lt=男大迹王|1=Emperor Keitai}}を祀ったのが始まりであるという。酒人小川真人の末裔は古山に城を築き小川氏を称した。{{ill|lt=鎌倉時代|Q236205|qid=Q236205|1=Kamakura period}}に入ると{{ill|lt=小川貞綱|UNKNOWN|lt=小川左衛門貞綱}}が{{ill|lt=承久の乱|Q1372308|qid=Q1372308|1=Jōkyū War}}の戦功によって{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=小川荘|1=UNKNOWN}}{{ill|lt=地頭|Q1329805|qid=Q1329805|1=Jitō}}職や{{ill|lt=小川城|Q11460417|qid=Q11460417|1=小川城}}主として小川郷3000石を領し、社殿を修築した。{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=応仁・文明の乱|1=UNKNOWN}}で小川氏が敗退すると社殿は廃れたものの、{{ill|lt=天文 (元号)|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=天文|1=Tenbun}}5年（{{ill|lt=1536年|Q6457|qid=Q6457|1=1536}}）には{{ill|lt=大日方長政|UNKNOWN|lt=大日方弾正正忠小五郎長政}}が小川村を領するようになったために再興した。また、かつての鎮座地は現在地に隣接する丘の上の宮平にあり、観月の名所と謳われたが、大日方氏が現在地に造営して鎮座し、かつての鎮座地には御射山神社が残り、その後に御射山神社地境内地は校舎用地となりて当社に合祀した。{{ill|lt=慶長|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185|1=Keichō}}3年（{{ill|lt=1598年|Q6800|qid=Q6800|1=1598}}）に{{ill|lt=上杉景勝|Q1376605|qid=Q1376605|1=Uesugi Kagekatsu}}が{{ill|lt=会津|Q1205071|qid=Q1205071|1=Aizu}}に移封となった際には、{{ill|lt=大日方氏|Q11435635|qid=Q11435635|1=大日方氏}}も{{ill|lt=浪人|Q212418|qid=Q212418|1=Rōnin}}となり当地に土着し、古山城は廃城となり社家数戸も散亡してしまった。{{ill|lt=寛政|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131|1=Kansei}}2年（{{ill|lt=1790年|Q7775|qid=Q7775|1=1790}}）8月には{{ill|lt=吉田家|Q11413722|qid=Q11413722|1=Yoshida family}}に社号宣旨を願い、告文を受けて社号を大宮大明神・諏訪大明神宮から小川神社へと変更した。{{ill|lt=明治|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096|1=Meiji era}}2年（{{ill|lt=1869年|Q7720|qid=Q7720|1=1869}}）1月には{{ill|lt=華頂宮|Q11620129|qid=Q11620129|1=Kachō-no-miya}}の御祈願所となり、裏菊御紋幕や提灯、紫小幕等を拝領した。同5年（{{ill|lt=1872年|Q7753|qid=Q7753|1=1872}}）には2石の社領を上知し、同6年（{{ill|lt=1873年|Q7757|qid=Q7757|1=1873}}）6月に村社に列し、{{ill|lt=大正|Q329174|qid=Q329174|1=Taishō era}}9年（{{ill|lt=1920年|Q2155|qid=Q2155|1=1920}}）11月30日に郷社に昇格した<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>。
現在の御本殿の創建は{{ill|lt=享保|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048|1=Kyōhō}}14年（{{ill|lt=1729年|Q6952|qid=Q6952|1=1729}}）10月の造営で、本殿覆屋・幣殿拝殿は{{ill|lt=昭和|Q327567|qid=Q327567|1=Shōwa era}}31年（{{ill|lt=1956年|Q5221|qid=Q5221|1=1956}}）に新しく築造された<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>。

{{ill|lt=小川村|Q1348971|qid=Q1348971|1=Ogawa, Nagano}}には{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=沢之宮小川神社|1=UNKNOWN}}も存在して{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}の論社であるが、{{ill|lt=明和|Q1146161|qid=Q1146161|1=Meiwa}}5年（{{ill|lt=1768年|Q7675|qid=Q7675|1=1768}}）4月付の文書によると両小川神社の神官（酒井長門）も氏子も祭神も同一であり、創建の前後は不明であるものの里宮・奥宮として一体であったと考えられる<ref>戸谷一郎『精説長野県史』123頁（日本精神文化研究所、1962年）</ref>。
